judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch conditional ('if (1) ... or (2) ...; otherwise, cash discounts shall accrue to the Contractor') followed by an unconditional rule for trade discounts and rebates. The split between cash discounts and trade discounts, and the duty to 'make provisions so that they can be secured', leave some room to argue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 9.1.1, which forbids the Contractor from taking any discount for its own benefit without seven days' notice and an opportunity for the Owner to fund it; that materially narrows the 'otherwise' branch here. Real interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence crediting mechanic tied to Paragraph 9.1. Plain and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 9.1 and 7.4.2 (proceeds of surplus material sales credited to the Owner); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Work the Contractor 'does not customarily perform with the Contractor's own personnel' must be subcontracted — 'customarily' is undefined and self-referential to the Contractor's own practice. The Owner's power to designate bidders sits against the Contractor's right to refuse anyone to whom it has 'reasonable objection'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 5.2.1-5.2.3, where the Contractor proposes subcontractors and the Owner may object, and against A201 5.2.3's rule on Contract Sum adjustment; the Agreement's Owner-selects model and A201's Contractor-proposes model are not the same. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-element condition followed by a Change Order remedy measured by the difference between two bid amounts. The elements are precise; 'without reservations or exceptions' is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price the Change Order would adjust is 'N/A', and against A201 5.2.3; the adjustment mechanism lacks a baseline. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'One calendar month ending on the last day of the month, or as follows:' with the alternative left blank; the default therefore governs. Minimal ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.3 (application and payment dates) and A201 9.3.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The payment-timing fill-ins are incomplete or garbled — 'not later than the ___ day of a month', 'not later than the first day of the following month', and '___ days after the Architect receives the Application'. A payment deadline with missing numbers is a mechanical defect that changes what the clause requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.6.1 and 9.7.1 (which lets the Contractor stop work if not paid 'within seven days after the date established in the Contract Documents') and First Addendum 12.2.2; the stop-work right depends on a date this clause fails to fix. Real relational problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A substantiation formula requiring cash disbursements to 'equal or exceed' a three-part computation, plus 'any other evidence required by the Owner or Architect'. The open-ended evidence requirement is the only soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.4 [New], which adds subcontractor statements, lien waivers and 'such other information ... as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require'; the two sets of requirements stack rather than conflict, though the reasonableness qualifier differs. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The schedule of values shall allocate the entire Guaranteed Maximum Price among the various portions of the Work' — clear as drafted, with the Fee shown as a single separate item. The internal wording is not the problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the Guaranteed Maximum Price is 'N/A': there is no sum to allocate, so the schedule of values that the entire progress-payment mechanism rests on has no defined content. That is a direct whole-instrument incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 'lesser of' formula whose second limb divides expense incurred by 'the share of the Guaranteed Maximum Price allocated to that portion of the Work'. The formula itself is arithmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A') and 12.1.5; the denominator of the formula does not exist. Serious relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory line ('the amount of each progress payment shall be computed as follows'), heavily truncated in this text. Nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the six sub-clauses that follow and 12.1.5; the structure holds. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A computation taking 'that portion of the Guaranteed Maximum Price properly allocable to completed Work'; 'properly allocable' is soft but the method is spelled out. Modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A'), 12.1.5 and 12.1.6; with no GMP figure this step cannot be performed as written. Strong relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds the portion of the GMP allocable to stored materials, with off-site storage conditioned on advance approval and a written location agreement. Clear conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A'), 7.5.6 and A201 9.3.2; again the GMP referent is missing, though the storage conditions themselves harmonise. Moderate to high.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The retainage percentage is filled in as 'N/A percent (N/A %)', and the fee-computation alternative depends on 'a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion' — a blank rate plus an estimate-based ratio. Both are nameable defects on the face of the clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.7.3 [Revision], which sets retainage at five percent (5%); the base agreement's 'N/A' and the Addendum's 5% sit in the same instrument and must be reconciled. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subtract the aggregate of previous payments made by the Owner' — arithmetic and definite. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.2.3, which uses the identical step on termination; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts a shortfall 'indicated by the Contractor' or 'resulting from errors subsequently discovered by the Owner's accountants'; the second limb gives the Owner's own accountants a unilateral deduction trigger. That one-sidedness is a modest contra proferentem point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.4 (the substantiation it references) and 12.1.9/12.2.3 (Owner's accountants acting 'in the sole interest of the Owner'); the scheme is internally consistent even if one-sided. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Subtracts amounts for which the Architect withheld or nullified a Certificate under A201 9.5. Simple cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.5.1's enumerated withholding grounds; the cross-reference works. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sets subcontractor retainage at 'not less than ten percent (10%)' but leaves the review and approval procedure to a future 'mutually acceptable' agreement — an agreement to agree. The clause is also mis-numbered 12.1.9 rather than 12.1.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.1.7.3, which sets the Contractor's own retainage at 5%, and against the following provision also numbered 12.1.9; the duplicate numbering and mismatched retainage rates are a genuine drafting inconsistency. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A protective clause limiting what the Architect's certification represents; long but conventional and internally consistent. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.2 (which makes the same disclaimers) and the preceding provision that also bears the number 12.1.9; the duplicate numbering is the only real issue. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory conditions clause: final payment 'constituting the entire unpaid balance of the Contract Sum' is due when two conditions are met. 'Entire unpaid balance of the Contract Sum' is only as clear as the Contract Sum itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.1 [New], which adds a third condition (recorded Notice of Completion), and against 5.1.1/5.2.1 where the Contract Sum has no stated figure. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fully performed the Contract except for the Contractor's responsibility to correct Work ... and to satisfy other requirements, if any, which extend beyond final payment' — 'other requirements, if any' is an unnamed residual category. Modest general-versus-specific softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 12.2.2 and 9.10.2's list of submittals; the residual category is filled by those provisions. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A final Certificate for Payment has been issued by the Architect' — a single, verifiable event. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.2.3 and A201 9.10.1; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No later than 30 days after the issuance of the Architect's final Certificate for Payment, or as follows:' with the alternative line left empty. The trailing invitation to state something else, unanswered, is a small gap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 12.2.2 [Revision], which substitutes 'within fifty (50) days after recordation of the Notice of Completion or within five (5) business days after ... a lien-free endorsement, whichever is earlier'; the 30-day rule and the 50-day rule cannot both govern. Direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sequenced accounting and certification timetable ending with an express statement that its time periods 'supersede those stated in Subparagraph 9.4.1' of A201. Clear, if elaborate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.4.1 (seven days) and 9.10.1, and against First Addendum 12.2.2; the express supersession handles A201 9.4.1 but not the Addendum's separate final-payment timetable. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Creates a 30-day arbitration demand deadline whose lapse makes the Owner's accountants' figure 'binding on the Contractor'. A short forfeiture window running from receipt of a certificate is exactly the kind of term parties fight about, and 'the disputed amount' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 4.4.6, 4.5.1 (mandatory mediation as a condition precedent) and 4.6.1-4.6.3; this clause lets the Contractor demand arbitration 'without a further decision of the Architect', which sits awkwardly with A201's Architect-decision-then-mediation sequence. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Post-final-payment correction costs are reimbursed 'but not in excess of the Guaranteed Maximum Price', and savings are to be 'recalculated' if the Contractor 'has participated in savings as provided in Paragraph 5.2'. Both qualifiers depend on things this Agreement never fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1, where the GMP is 'N/A' and the bracketed invitation to insert savings-participation provisions was left blank; the clause conditions itself on two absent terms. Strong relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Caps convenience-termination payment at the for-cause amount 'except that the Contractor's Fee shall be calculated as if the Work had been fully completed', including 'a reasonable estimate of the Cost of the Work for Work not actually completed'. The estimate standard is soft, and the interplay of cap and exception is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 14.4.3, which entitles the Contractor on convenience termination to payment for Work executed plus 'reasonable overhead and profit on the Work not executed', and A201 14.1.3; the Agreement's cap and A201's entitlement point different ways. Real conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A cap on for-cause termination payment expressed as 'shall not cause the Guaranteed Maximum Price to be exceeded, nor shall it exceed an amount calculated as follows'. The double cap is clear in structure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 (GMP 'N/A') and A201 14.2.4, which measures the outcome against 'the unpaid balance of the Contract Sum'; the first limb of the cap has no referent and the two measures differ. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Take the Cost of the Work incurred by the Contractor to the date of termination' — a single arithmetic step. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 7's definition of the Cost of the Work; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Computes the fee at 'the rate stated in Subparagraph 5.1.2 or, if the Contractor's Fee is stated as a fixed sum ... an amount that bears the same ratio ... to a reasonable estimate of the probable Cost of the Work upon its completion'. The estimate is undefined and unassigned to any party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.1.2, where the Fee is a flat $380,000 with no rate, so only the second limb can operate; 12.1.7.3 uses the same untethered 'reasonable estimate'. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subtract the aggregate of previous payments made by the Owner.' Definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 12.1.7.4; identical mechanic. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fair compensation, either by purchase or rental at the election of the Owner' for retained equipment — 'fair compensation' is an open valuation standard with no mechanism for fixing it. Nameable but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 13.2.1 (which it excepts) and A201 5.4.1 (contingent assignment of subcontracts) and 14.2.2; the assignment machinery aligns. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: On suspension the GMP and Contract Time 'shall be increased as provided in Subparagraph 14.3.2 of A201 except that the term
shall be understood to mean the Contractor's Fee'. The redefinition is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 5.2.1 ('N/A' GMP), 5.1.2 and 6.4; an instruction to increase a maximum price that does not exist cannot be applied. Real defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reading rule: references to A201 mean that provision 'as amended or supplemented by other provisions of the Contract Documents'. Broad but purposive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Supplementary Conditions preamble, which says unaltered provisions of the General Conditions remain in effect; the two reinforce each other. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Interest runs 'at the rate stated below, or in the absence thereof, at the legal rate prevailing ... at the place where the Project is located', and the rate line appears blank or garbled. The fallback saves it, but the blank is a nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 9.7.1, which adds interest 'as provided for in the Contract Documents' to stop-work costs; the fallback supplies a rate. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens' and 'Mary Williamson' as the Owner's representative without saying whether they act jointly or severally. The plural designation without an allocation rule is a genuine ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 14.3 [Revised] ('Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson') and Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1 ('The Owner's authorized representative is Mary Williamson', but actions may be taken by 'Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson'); three provisions name the representative differently. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Contractor's representative is given as 'John F. Maurer, EME, succeeded by Keith H. Willis, Senior Project Manager' — a designation with a built-in, undated succession. Mildly indeterminate as to when the succession took effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.5, which forbids changing a representative without ten days' written notice; a pre-built succession sits oddly with that requirement. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Neither the Owner's nor the Contractor's representative shall be changed without ten days' written notice to the other party.' Definite and symmetrical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 14.3/14.4 and Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1, which name a different set of Owner actors; whether the SC designation is a 'change' requiring notice is left open. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other provisions:' followed by nothing — a heading with no content. There is no term to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 8.1.1, which excepts personnel costs 'as may be provided in Article 14', and against First Addendum 14.6 [New] (representations and warranties); the blank leaves the 8.1.1 exception dangling and the Addendum uses the same number for a different subject. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory enumeration line excluding later Modifications. Plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Article 1 and A201 1.1.1, which excludes documents not 'specifically enumerated in the Agreement'; consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identifies the Agreement as the executed 1997 edition of A111. Simple identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 15.1.1 [Revision], which restates it 'as modified by the First Addendum hereto'; the unrevised text omits the Addendum. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text identifies the General Conditions as 'the 1991 edition of the General Conditions of the Contract for Construction AIA Document A201-1997' — the stated edition year contradicts the document number in the same sentence. That is a mechanical error going to which document is incorporated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against First Addendum 15.1.2 [Revision] and the Supplementary Conditions preamble, both of which identify A201, 1997 Edition; the '1991' reference is inconsistent with them. Real inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Points to Specifications 'contained in the Project Manual dated as in Subparagraph 15.1.3' with the section/title/page table left empty. The incorporation is by reference to an undescribed volume.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 15.1.3, whose Project Manual date is blank and whose document list reads 'TBD'; the incorporation chain terminates in nothing. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Drawings are as follows, and are dated ___ unless a different date is shown below', with the list left blank or 'TBD'. An unlisted, undated set of Drawings is a real gap in identifying the Work.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.1.5 and 1.1.1 (documents must be 'specifically enumerated in the Agreement'), and against First Addendum 6.5/Supplementary Conditions 3.10.5, which contemplate drawings being developed later; the enumeration and the fast-track model do not fit together. Genuine tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists the First Addendum and the Supplementary Conditions as 'Addenda', then excludes bidding-requirement portions unless enumerated. Calling the negotiated Addendum an 'Addendum' is loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against 15.1.2 and the Supplementary Conditions preamble, which treat those documents as modifications of the General Conditions rather than as bidding addenda; the classification affects the precedence analysis under Article 1. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates Exhibits A through E, one of which (Exhibit E) is a certificate of insurance rather than a contractual term. Listing an evidentiary certificate as a Contract Document is odd but not ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Exhibits A, B, C and D, which set rates and tax treatments that cut across Article 7 and 8, and against Article 1's precedence rule; making the rate sheets Contract Documents is what gives them operative force. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ARTICLE 16 INSURANCE AND BONDS' followed only by the bracketed AIA instruction — no limits of liability, no bonds, nothing filled in. A wholly empty article on a subject the form requires to be completed is a nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 11.1.2, which requires insurance written for 'not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law, whichever coverage is greater', and against Supplementary Conditions 11.4.1.1.1 and 11.6; the specified limits the General Conditions assume simply do not exist. Real incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard execution recital as to counterparts and delivery. Nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 1.5.1 (Contract Documents to be signed by Owner and Contractor); consistent. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital that the Addendum is 'attached to and incorporated by reference' in the Agreement 'dated February 1, 2002', for the purpose of 'modifying, supplementing, and amending certain terms'. The recital's date is stated with precision the Agreement's own date line lacks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against the Agreement's opening date line, which is incomplete in this instrument, and against the Addendum's unexecuted signature block ('this __ day of ___, 2002'); a recital fixing a date that the operative execution block leaves blank is a classic recital-versus-operative mismatch. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds duties to furnish 'only skilled and properly trained staff' and to designate one supervisory employee who 'personally shall supervise and attend to the Work', who may take other work 'only to the extent it does not impair his or her ability to perform this Work'. 'Impair', 'properly trained' and 'personally' are all soft standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 3.9.1 (competent superintendent in attendance at the site) and 3.4.3; the revised Article 2 layers a further requirement on top rather than contradicting it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The date of commencement of the work shall be July 15, 2002, pending approval of permits' — 'pending approval of permits' is genuinely ambiguous as to whether the date is fixed or conditional, and if conditional, on whose permits and by when. That phrase is the nameable defect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against A201 8.1.2 ('the date established in the Agreement'), A201 8.2.2 (commencement not changed by insurance dates) and Agreement 4.2 (Contract Time measured from commencement); a floating commencement date destabilises the whole time scheme, including the November 30, 2003 completion date in 4.3. Real relational problem.
